original_test_intent: Validate SBR hot-reset interoperability on the approved HGX PCIe hierarchy by proving every NVQual Test #24 reset affects only the intended secondary-bus scope and returns all expected NVIDIA endpoints at required link state and functional health without hang, unplanned host reboot, or new errors.
original_method: Pin the upstream bridge and exact secondary-bus subtree, sibling blast radius, endpoint/driver quiesce, SBR assertion/deassertion primitive, iterations/timing, expected disappearance, retrain/re-enumeration, generation/width, driver/GPU recovery, and error contract; preserve baselines; durably record each complete reset transaction before the next; stop on first scope or recovery anomaly and use out-of-band recovery.
manual_activity: HGX owner/FAE approves the SBR hierarchy, expected endpoint disruption and long-run iteration policy; an operator isolates the SUT, supervises out-of-band state, and owns recovery if devices or host fail to return.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA NVQual Test #24 SBR interoperability package/configuration and compatible firmware/driver
Exact upstream bridge, secondary-bus subtree, root-port/switch/retimer/endpoints/GPUs and sibling topology
Driver/workload quiesce, SBR primitive, assertion/deassertion timing, expected disappearance, retrain/re-enumeration/link/function deadlines
Iteration count, error acceptance, persistent storage, abort, final-state, and recovery policy
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production HGX SUT with explicit SBR scope and service-impact authorization
No unsaved workload; consumers quiesced; verified BMC/console/power recovery
Validate bridge ownership and sibling blast radius before any write
Stop on wrong-scope reset, failed/late retrain, missing/misbound endpoint, downtraining, driver/GPU failure, hang/reboot, new AER, thermal/power fault, tool failure, or evidence gap
No forced rescan/rebind, escalation to power cycle, evidence clearing, or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate Test #24 configuration, hierarchy, baseline, quiesce, interlocks, ledger, and recovery
Run only the approved SBR primitive on the mapped bridge
Commit assertion, expected disappearance, deassertion, retrain/re-enumeration, identity/link/function/error results before another reset
Correlate PCIe, NVIDIA, driver, OS, BMC, console, thermal, and power health
Do not infer the bridge, broaden reset scope, force recovery, retry faults, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #24 SBR recipe, exact hierarchy/sibling scope, iterations, and service impact
Define quiesce, reset timing, expected disappearance/re-enumeration, link/function/error acceptance
Own first-fault disposition and out-of-band recovery
Review every reset transaction and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model each SBR as a scoped hierarchy transaction from quiesce and pre-state through bus reset, expected disappearance, link retrain, identity-complete endpoint and driver/GPU restoration, and health acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact bus scope, sibling containment, transaction phases, persistent evidence, first-fault inhibition, functional recovery, and out-of-band restoration.

review_improvement: Makes each SBR a scoped, identity-complete reset transaction and prevents recovered final enumeration or an escalated power cycle from masquerading as hot-reset interoperability.
independent_technical_reasoning: SBR acts on a downstream bus hierarchy rather than a single abstract GPU. Correctness therefore includes containment: the intended endpoints must reset and recover while out-of-scope siblings remain stable. Re-enumeration alone is insufficient because BDFs or driver bindings can change, links can downtrain, and reset errors can be transient. Each transaction must bind topology before and after by stable device identities and preserve reset-phase/error timing before another reset can overwrite the state.
